target_customer: Indian businesses that burn diesel: vehicle fleets, hospitals, generator operators and other B2B buyers
problem: Buying diesel and petrol for fleets and generators meant trips to stations, queues and weak quality assurance. Doorstep delivery by metered trucks removes that.
business_model: Fuel delivery with margin per litre plus delivery fee

founders.name: Nabin Roy
previous_startups: Earlier ventures in ed-tech and home services (outcomes not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder and describes him as a repeat entrepreneur with operations and strategy skills.

founders.name: Ashish Gupta
founders.background_notes: Named as founder by KrASIA (Aug 2019) and co-founder by DT Next (May 2021), not on the YC page. YC description mentions an ex-Shell founder with 9 years in oil marketing. Won USD 10,000 at the Wharton India Startup Challenge.

competitors.name: Reliance Industries
competitors.what: Large fuel retailer reported to be considering on-demand fuel delivery

competitors.name: Indian Oil, BPCL and HPCL
competitors.what: State oil marketing companies reported to be considering on-demand delivery

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering app, routing and metered tanker trucks. The hard parts were operational: vehicles, fuel safety and licensing.

defensibility.rationale: Fleet of refueling trucks and customer relationships helped, but large fuel companies and competitors such as FuelBuddy could replicate delivery.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents were reported to be weighing entry in 2019; the actual exit came from a direct rival, FuelBuddy, which bought the company in May 2021.

market_need_then: Indian fleets, hospitals and generator users relied on stations or bulk suppliers; KrASIA called it Uber for fuel and the company claimed demand across several cities.

branding.domain_note: mypetrolpump.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and descriptive; press called it Swiggy or Uber for fuel

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive and clear but generic, and no evidence of brand recognition beyond press analogies.

outcome_analysis: MyPetrolPump raised about USD 1.6M in 2019 and operated in Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune before FuelBuddy acquired it in an all cash and stock deal announced May 9, 2021. No post-seed round was found, so the sale looks like consolidation of a small doorstep fuel delivery business rather than a venture-scale exit; the price and reasons were not disclosed.
notes: YourStory pages returned 403 and were not worked around. Funding confirmed by search results from YourStory, Inc42 and KrASIA snippets plus the opened KrASIA article; round size also quoted as about 11 crore rupees. DT Next says total raised was Rs 14 crore; aggregators give $1.78M to $1.88M. Founders differ between YC (Nabin Roy only) and press (Ashish Gupta); both recorded. Failure factor is inferred from absence of later rounds and is weak.
